name: Intestinal Disease Due to Fat Malabsorption

criteria.description: Presence of steatorrhea confirmed by quantitative fecal fat analysis
Low serum levels of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K)
Abnormal results on fat absorption tests such as 72-hour fecal fat collection or breath tests
Clinical symptoms consistent with fat malabsorption including weight loss and diarrhea
Imaging or histological evidence of intestinal mucosal disease contributing to malabsorption

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of steatorrhea confirmed by fecal fat analysis plus at least one additional major criterion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of pancreatic insufficiency and other causes of malabsorption.

searchTerms: weight loss from poor nutrient absorption

common.symptomName: Fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies (A, D, E, K)
common.notes: May manifest as night blindness, osteomalacia, coagulopathy
searchTerms: lack of vitamins A, D, E, K

common.symptomName: Muscle weakness secondary to vitamin E deficiency
searchTerms: muscle weakness from vitamin E lack
weak muscles due to vitamin deficiency
low vitamin E causing muscle fatigue

occasional.symptomName: Peripheral neuropathy related to vitamin E deficiency
searchTerms: nerve damage from vitamin E lack
tingling or numbness due to vitamin E deficiency

occasional.symptomName: Easy bruising or bleeding due to vitamin K deficiency
searchTerms: easy bruising from vitamin K lack
bleeding tendency due to vitamin K deficiency
weakness due to lack of nutrients

rare.symptomName: Night blindness due to vitamin A deficiency
searchTerms: night blindness from vitamin A deficiency
edema due to poor protein absorption

laboratory: Elevated fecal fat on 72-hour stool collection
Low serum levels of vitamins A, D, E, and K
imaging: Abdominal ultrasound or CT may show intestinal mucosal abnormalities
Small bowel biopsy may reveal villous atrophy or mucosal damage
genetic: Mutations in genes related to fat absorption disorders (e.g., abetalipoproteinemia genes) if applicable
other: Positive fat absorption breath tests (e.g., 13C-triolein breath test)

distinguishingFeatures: Improvement with pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy
Histologic evidence of villous atrophy with crypt hyperplasia

redFlags: Severe malnutrition with rapid weight loss
Signs of fat-soluble vitamin deficiency complications (e.g., bleeding, neuropathy)
references: Orphanet: Intestinal disease due to fat malabsorption - ORPHA:104005
